reading.thesis: Cast an eight-mana Gishath off a dork-and-land ramp base, make one hit land, and let the reveal put Dinosaurs onto the battlefield in batches whose entry triggers pay in cards and bodies, until a committed trampling alpha ends it by commander damage.

lines.name: mana → ignition
lines.note: the cast: Mirari's Wake adds one mana per land tapped unconditionally; Regal Behemoth adds one per land only while you are the monarch, and loses it to any combat damage to you. Game 003's log has Wake doubling mana into Gishath and 'Regal' adding mana for the recast through tax (captain's log, not a stack)

lines.name: ignition → conversion
lines.note: one connect, simultaneous entries, one Uprising draw per entering power-4+ creature and one Pantlaza discover. Stack 001 resolved exactly this shape and passed, but its stipulated reveal names Ripjaw Raptor, Ravenous Sailback and Cultivate, none in this 99, so it is not cited (open_questions[0])

lines.name: fuel → ignition
lines.note: creatures stacked on top at instant speed before the swing make the reveal a chosen one. Oracle-derivable; no stack

lines.name: output → conversion
lines.note: the one-sided wipe, with Temple Altisaur (protection) as the enabler between the two ends: Altisaur prevents the Act down to 1 on each other Dinosaur, Wrathful redirects what was dealt. Stack 004 passed on this shape but its board holds Ripjaw Raptor, not in this 99, so it is not cited (open_questions[3])

lines.name: wincon → conversion
lines.note: the attack token's power is the greatest other attacker's, so with any 4-power attacker it is an entering power-4+ creature for Uprising and Vaultborn. Oracle-derivable; no stack

open_questions.question: Re-resolve stack 001's connect on a reveal drawn only from this 99 (e.g. Regisaur Alpha, Vaultborn Tyrant, Palani's Hatcher, Earthshaker Dreadmaw) with Pantlaza and Garruk's Uprising out.
open_questions.why_it_matters: No passing stack names only this 99's non-basic cards: 001's reveal stipulates Ripjaw Raptor, Ravenous Sailback and Cultivate; 004's board holds Ripjaw Raptor; 002, 003 and 005 hold Marauding Raptor, Polyraptor, Forerunner of the Empire, Ranging Raptors or Trapjaw Tyrant. The deck's core line is therefore unverified on v1.2.0, and every lines[].verified_by here is null.

open_questions.question: With Roaming Throne named Dinosaur, does Gishath's combat-damage trigger trigger an additional time (a second reveal off one hit), and how does Pantlaza's 'do this only once each turn' interact with Throne's extra trigger?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If yes, Roaming Throne multiplies the ignition itself rather than being one payoff among six, and lines[2] becomes the engine's spine.

open_questions.question: Berserkers' Onslaught (or Akroma's Will's double-strike mode, or Boros Charm's) on an attacking Gishath: two combat damage steps and two reveals? Do Dinosaurs revealed in the first-strike step (Devil Dinosaur, Regal Imperiosaur) raise the regular-step hit and so the second reveal?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It decides whether the v1.2.0 double-strike add belongs in the ignition or only in the alpha.

open_questions.question: Re-resolve stack 004 without Ripjaw Raptor: Blasphemous Act with Temple Altisaur, Wrathful Raptors and Gishath out.
open_questions.why_it_matters: goldfish_targets' 'one-sided wipe' route still names stack 004 in its label; on this 99 that line is a claim until a board of its own cards passes.

open_questions.question: Does the goldfish read Roaming Throne's trigger doubling on Gishath's reveal, and Berserkers' Onslaught's double strike as two reveals? model-coverage lists both as 'seen' on bodies/combat/target, which does not say either effect is modelled.
open_questions.why_it_matters: A card the model cannot read looks exactly like a card that does not help: two v1.2.0 adds that multiply the ignition may be read as a 4/4 and an enchantment.

open_questions.question: Nature's Lore, Three Visits and Skyshroud Claim are 'invisible' in model-coverage (no channel reads them) yet sit in the required 'Ramp or fixing drawn' group. Are they modelled as land drops at all?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The required group's assembled figures count them as ramp drawn; if the model plays them as nothing, the group overstates the mana stage.

findings.claim: Knight of the Stampede, Otepec Huntmaster and Urza's Incubator named Dinosaur discount every Dinosaur spell, Gishath included. Hunting Velociraptor's prowl {2}{R} applies only after a Dinosaur has dealt combat damage to a player this turn, so for Gishath it is a re-cast discount, not a first-cast one.
findings.note: Round-2 over-claim resolved. The three static reducers match their oracles: Knight '{2} less', Otepec '{1} less', Incubator '{2} less' for the chosen type. Velociraptor now has its own sentence, gated on prior combat damage, which matches its oracle ('if you dealt combat damage to a player this turn with a creature with any of its creature types'). Pedantic only: the gate is any creature sharing a type with the spell, so for Gishath an Avatar would also qualify, but the 99 has none, so 'a Dinosaur' is exact for this deck. Commander tax still stacks on the prowl cost, and 'discount' does not deny that. Length is 1391, under the cap. The audit figures in the stage (0.696 / 0.906 / 2.018) are unchanged from round 2, where they were re-derived. Mechanically checkable: flag a card whose oracle carries 'prowl' or 'if you dealt combat damage ... this turn' when it shares a sentence with 'cost(s) ... less' or 'discount' and no conditional word ('only', 'after', 'if').

findings.claim: Quartzwood Crasher makes an X/X token where X is all the combat damage your trampling creatures dealt that player (with Uprising's trample, the whole connect)
findings.note: Round-2 wording note resolved. The oracle reads 'create an X/X ... where X is the amount of damage those creatures dealt to that player', with 'those creatures' meaning creatures you control with trample. Garruk's Uprising grants all your creatures trample, so 'the whole connect' is right. Length is 1263. The rest of the stage is unchanged from round 2: Wrathful Raptors at 0.071 / 0.172, one of two SPOFs, and the Roaming Throne reading still conditional and routed to open_questions[1].

findings.claim: Altisaur prevents the Act down to 1 on each other Dinosaur, Wrathful redirects what was dealt. Stack 004 passed on this shape but its board holds Ripjaw Raptor ... so it is not cited (open_questions[3])
findings.note: Still dashed (verified_by null), and the reason for not citing 004 is stated. 'Each other Dinosaur' scopes Temple Altisaur correctly: its oracle says 'another Dinosaur you control', so Altisaur takes the full 13. Strictly, 'redirects' is loose. Wrathful Raptors' oracle has the damaged Dinosaur deal 'that much damage' again to a non-Dinosaur target, so the original damage is still dealt and nothing is moved. stages[4] says this exactly ('dealt again'), so the model is right overall and the note is shorthand. It does not assert anything the oracle denies, so it does not count toward the verdict. Every clause is oracle-direct and the line stays dashed, so this is not a claim dressed up as a disclaimer.

findings.claim: the stack has to be built ON the swing turn ... the window is after those, in the declare-attackers or declare-blockers step before damage
findings.note: Round-1 timing finding resolved. Bonehoard Dracosaur's oracle exiles the top two in your upkeep. The draw step takes one. Etali's trigger reads 'Whenever Etali attacks', so it resolves in declare attackers. Congregation at Dawn and Worldly Tutor are instants. Precombat main also works when Etali is not attacking, which the prose leaves out. That is incomplete, not wrong.

findings.claim: Enlightened Tutor is a draw tutor, not a reveal tutor ... one left on top only spends a reveal slot and goes to the bottom
findings.note: Round-1 over-claim resolved. Roaming Throne is an Artifact Creature, Golem. Onslaught, Wake and Uprising are enchantments. Gishath's oracle puts only 'Dinosaur creature cards' onto the battlefield and 'the rest on the bottom'.

findings.claim: Bonehoard ... in each of your upkeeps; Etali exiles the top card of each library only when it attacks
findings.note: Round-1 finding resolved. Matches both oracles.

findings.claim: a claim awaiting a stack ... his combat-damage trigger would trigger an additional time
findings.note: Round-1 over-claim resolved. The note and stages[3] ('Read off the oracle text that would cover ... no stack has resolved it') are now both conditional and point to open_questions[1]. Roaming Throne's oracle reads 'a triggered ability of another creature you control of the chosen type', and Gishath is a Dinosaur Avatar, so the reading is plausible and is still correctly left as a claim.

findings.claim: Kinjalli's Sunwing ... (oracle text, no log: game 001's 'makes their creatures enter tapped' was played on V3, before Sunwing came in)
findings.note: Round-1 mis-cite resolved. captains_log.json games_considered puts 001 on version 3. Its what_changed lists Kinjalli's Sunwing among the V3-to-V4 adds. The oracle reads 'Creatures your opponents control enter tapped.' Side note, not a defect of this model: log 001 credits an enter-tapped effect on a list that did not run Sunwing, which is an inconsistency inside the log record.

findings.claim: Overwhelming Stampede gives every creature you control trample and +X/+X, X the greatest power among them
findings.note: Round-1 mis-cite resolved.

findings.claim: Mirari's Wake adds one mana per land tapped unconditionally; Regal Behemoth ... only while you are the monarch
findings.note: Round-1 over-claim resolved. Matches both oracles. The game-003 citation holds: log.jsonl 003 has Wake doubling mana and 'Regal, like something ... doubles my mana ... bring Gishath back with Comma[nder tax]'. stages[0] now gives Hulking Raptor as 'a fixed {G}{G} ... which does not scale', which matches its oracle.

findings.claim: The label is a uniqueness fallback, not a reading ... only Atzocan Seer carries 'recursion'
findings.note: Round-1 contradicts-artifact finding resolved. deck_map.json gives all six city-5 cards ramp:dork and threat:body. Only Atzocan Seer has 'recursion', and Intrepid Paleontologist is hate:graveyard.

findings.claim: With Temple Altisaur out it is one-sided for your other Dinosaurs, which take 1 each; Altisaur ... takes the full 13 itself, and with Wrathful Raptors every one of those amounts, Altisaur's 13 the largest, is dealt again to a non-Dinosaur target
findings.note: This is the new Altisaur text, and it is correct. Temple Altisaur's oracle reads 'damage to another Dinosaur you control', so it does not protect itself. Wrathful Raptors (a 5/5 Dinosaur, so it survives at 1) triggers on 'a Dinosaur you control is dealt damage'. Stack 004's final_state redirects 13 of the 16 by last known information, as round 1 recorded. 'One-sided for your other Dinosaurs' scopes it correctly: the non-Dinosaur mana creatures (Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Selvala, Lorekeeper, Paleontologist, Seer, Drover, Knight, Otepec) all die. The round-1 under-claim ('each of those 1s is redirected') is fixed. Not citing 004 follows the main session's policy, and open_questions[3] carries it.

findings.claim: Akroma's Will's first mode and Boros Charm's third grant double strike for one turn, and they sit in protection
findings.note: This answers round 1's FYI. Akroma's Will's first mode: 'Creatures you control gain flying, vigilance, and double strike until end of turn.' Boros Charm's third mode: 'Target creature gains double strike until end of turn.' Mode numbering is correct. Leaving them in stages[5] with a cross-reference is consistent with the stage's card list, and stages[5] describes Akroma's Will's two-mode commander clause correctly.

findings.claim: double strike on a pumped Gishath (Onslaught here; Akroma's Will and Boros Charm grant it too): two combat damage steps, two reveals ... Unverified
findings.note: Hedged, and open_questions[2] now names all three sources. The two-trigger reading is standard (a double-striker deals combat damage in both steps), so it is a safe claim to leave dashed. The open sub-question is real: Devil Dinosaur ('Other Dinosaurs you control get +1/+1') and Regal Imperiosaur revealed in the first-strike step would raise Gishath's regular-step damage, and with it the second reveal.

findings.claim: Gishath, Sun's Avatar
findings.note: Unchanged from round 1 and still sound. Sunfrill Imitator needs 'another target Dinosaur you control'.

findings.claim: declared ramp group (15 cards) at 0.696 in the opening seven and drawn by turn six in 0.906, mean turn 2.018
findings.note: A fresh deck-audit run gives engine.targets[0]: 15 components, opening_seven 0.696, by_turn_6_rate 0.906, mean_turn 2.018.

findings.claim: Wrathful Raptors alone 0.071 opening seven, 0.172 by turn six; one of two SPOFs
findings.note: A fresh deck-audit gives single_points_of_failure[0] as odds.opening_seven 0.071, measured.by_turn_6_rate 0.172. [1] is Blasphemous Act.

findings.claim: Act alone 0.071; pair by turn six 0.020, mean turn 7.852
findings.note: A fresh deck-audit gives targets[6]: two components at 0.071 each, by_turn_6_rate 0.02, mean_turn 7.852.

findings.claim: five-card protection group 0.312 opening seven, 0.526 by turn six
findings.note: A fresh deck-audit gives targets[5]: 5 components, 0.312, 0.526. Do not confuse it with targets[1] (cost reducer, also 5 cards and 0.312, but 0.525).

findings.note: Re-enumerated from cards.json: 28 non-commander cards with 'Creature' and 'Dinosaur' in the type line. Roaming Throne is a Golem.

v1_stages.label: THE EIGHT-MANA CLIMB
v1_stages.what_it_does: Pays for an eight-mana commander, then for the Dinosaurs he did not reveal. Three layers: every land but Kessig Wolf Run, plus Sol Ring and Arcane Signet; land search (Nature's Lore, Three Visits, Skyshroud Claim, Huatli's basic); and since v1.2.0 a crop of mana creatures (Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Drover of the Mighty, Ixalli's Lorekeeper, Intrepid Paleontologist, Atzocan Seer) above the big producers: Selvala (X equal to the greatest power you control), Mirari's Wake (one extra mana per land tapped), Regal Behemoth (one extra per land tapped, but only while you are the monarch, which combat damage to you takes away) and Hulking Raptor (a fixed {G}{G} each first main phase, which does not scale). Knight of the Stampede, Otepec Huntmaster and Urza's Incubator named Dinosaur discount every Dinosaur spell, Gishath included. Hunting Velociraptor's prowl {2}{R} applies only after a Dinosaur has dealt combat damage to a player this turn, so for Gishath it is a re-cast discount, not a first-cast one. Much of the colour is creature-only: Ixalli's Lorekeeper, Ancient Ziggurat, and Cavern, Secluded Courtyard and Unclaimed Territory named Dinosaur pay for Gishath but not for Overwhelming Stampede or Akroma's Will. deck-audit prices the declared ramp group (15 cards, not this whole stage) at 0.696 in the opening seven and drawn by turn six in 0.906 of games, mean turn 2.018.
cards: Huatli, Poet of Unity // Roar of the Fifth People

v1_stages.label: THE FIRST CONNECT
v1_stages.what_it_does: Nothing in the deck is the engine until Gishath deals combat damage to a player: the trigger reveals that many cards and puts every Dinosaur among them onto the battlefield. Two things must resolve: the cast (eight mana, the stage above) and the hit. He has haste, vigilance and trample on his own card, so the connect needs size and a second count, not haste. Berserkers' Onslaught gives attackers double strike: two combat damage steps, two triggers (open_questions[2]); Akroma's Will's first mode and Boros Charm's third grant double strike for one turn, and they sit in protection because that is the mode they are usually held for. Sunfrill Imitator, attacking, can become a copy of Gishath and carry the same trigger, which the pilot's game 003 records happening (a log, not a stack). Kessig Wolf Run is a repeatable land pump: the reveal counts damage dealt, so every point that gets through is one more card. Gishath lives in the command zone, so he can never be revealed or tutored, and he is the stage's single point of failure; each removal costs commander tax rather than the card. The reveal is a PUT, not a cast: Zacama's 'if you cast it' untap does nothing through this door. No passing stack on this 99 resolves a connect (open_questions[0]).

v1_stages.label: WHAT THE TOP OF THE LIBRARY HOLDS
v1_stages.what_it_does: The reveal is only as good as the top of the library, and the 99 holds 28 Dinosaurs for it to find (Roaming Throne is a Golem in the library and does not count). Congregation at Dawn and Worldly Tutor put creatures on TOP at instant speed, and the stack has to be built ON the swing turn: cast earlier, your draw step takes the top card and Bonehoard Dracosaur's upkeep exiles two more, and Etali's attack trigger exiles one more, so the window is after those, in the declare-attackers or declare-blockers step before damage. Enlightened Tutor is a draw tutor, not a reveal tutor: its targets (Roaming Throne, Berserkers' Onslaught, Mirari's Wake, Garruk's Uprising) are not Dinosaur creature cards, so one left on top only spends a reveal slot and goes to the bottom; it is cast before your draw step. Natural Order eats a green mana creature for a green fatty straight onto the battlefield. Rishkar's Expertise draws off the greatest power on the board. Bonehoard Dracosaur exiles two off the top in each of your upkeeps for you to play; Etali exiles the top card of each library only when it attacks. Pugnacious Hammerskull is a cheap 6/6, power the payoffs count. There is no fodder stage: the creature sacrifices in the 99 are Natural Order's additional cost, Palani's Hatcher eating its own Eggs, and Atzocan Seer and Thrashing Brontodon sacrificing themselves. None is a theme.

v1_stages.label: WHAT AN ENTRY IS WORTH
v1_stages.what_it_does: Turns each Dinosaur that arrives, revealed or cast, into cards, bodies or damage. Garruk's Uprising draws per entering creature of power 4 or greater and gives trample; Vaultborn Tyrant draws and gains 3 on the same condition; Earthshaker Dreadmaw draws one per other Dinosaur; Trumpeting Carnosaur discovers 5; Pantlaza discovers once a turn at the entering creature's toughness. Curious Altisaur draws per Dinosaur that deals combat damage to a player and Quartzwood Crasher makes an X/X token where X is all the combat damage your trampling creatures dealt that player (with Uprising's trample, the whole connect). Roaming Throne named Dinosaur makes a triggered ability of another Dinosaur you control trigger an additional time. Read off the oracle text that would cover Pantlaza, Vaultborn, Earthshaker, Wrathful Raptors and Gishath's own reveal, a second reveal off one hit; that last is the claim this model leans on most and no stack has resolved it (open_questions[1]). It never covers Garruk's Uprising, an enchantment. Wrathful Raptors converts damage dealt to your Dinosaurs into damage at a non-Dinosaur; deck-audit prices it alone at 0.071 in the opening seven, drawn by turn six in 0.172, and it is one of the brief's two single points of failure.

v1_stages.label: WHAT THE BODIES POINT AT
v1_stages.what_it_does: The removal suite, most of it riding on Dinosaurs so a reveal can deliver it free: Bronzebeak Foragers exiles a nonland permanent from each opponent, Itzquinth makes a Dinosaur fight-without-fighting, Thrashing Brontodon and Tranquil Frillback answer artifacts and enchantments (Frillback also exiles a graveyard). Swords to Plowshares and Path to Exile are the cheap instants. Blasphemous Act is the reset: thirteen to every creature, near-free on a full table. With Temple Altisaur out it is one-sided for your other Dinosaurs, which take 1 each; Altisaur protects only OTHER Dinosaurs, so it takes the full 13 itself, and with Wrathful Raptors every one of those amounts, Altisaur's 13 the largest, is dealt again to a non-Dinosaur target. That line was resolved by stack 004 on a board that also held Ripjaw Raptor, which v1.2.0 does not run, so under the non-basic rule it is not cited here (open_questions[3]). deck-audit prices the Act alone at 0.071 in the opening seven and the declared Act-plus-Altisaur pair drawn by turn six in 0.020 of games, mean turn 7.852.

v1_stages.label: KEEPING THE BOARD THROUGH THE ANSWER
v1_stages.what_it_does: Tables wipe this deck, and the pilot's best games rebuilt faster than the table answered. Flawless Maneuver is free with a commander out; Heroic Intervention, Boros Charm's indestructible mode and Akroma's Will (both modes with a commander, including double strike and flying) cover destroy effects; Eerie Interlude blinks the board out of a wipe, and its end-step return is a simultaneous entry that fires every entry payoff in conversion. Temple Altisaur prevents all but 1 of any damage to your other Dinosaurs, a damage wipe included, but not to itself. Devil Dinosaur gives other Dinosaurs hexproof and +1/+1. Kinjalli's Sunwing makes opposing creatures enter tapped, so an opponent's haste creature cannot attack the turn it arrives (oracle text, no log: game 001's 'makes their creatures enter tapped' was played on V3, before Sunwing came in). deck-audit prices the declared five-card protection group at 0.312 in the opening seven and held by turn six in 0.526 of games.

v1_stages.label: THE COMMITTED ALPHA
v1_stages.what_it_does: Games end by commander damage or a wide trampling swing, and the pilot's log says both losses were a board that was ahead and attacks that were not committed. Overwhelming Stampede gives every creature you control trample and +X/+X, X the greatest power among them, Rydia's Return adds +3/+3 (or regrows two permanents), Regal Imperiosaur is a Dinosaur lord. Regisaur Alpha and Palani's Hatcher give other Dinosaurs haste, so the ones you CAST swing that turn; Gishath's reveal comes after attackers are declared, so revealed arrivals swing next turn. Ghalta and Mavren makes an attacking token as large as the greatest other attacker, Ghalta, Primal Hunger costs less per point of power, Carnage Tyrant is an uncounterable hexproof 7/6 trampler and Zacama a 9/9 trampler. Zacama's {2}{R} also pings a creature, one of four cards in the 99 that can damage your own Dinosaur for Wrathful Raptors, with Blasphemous Act, Itzquinth and Trumpeting Carnosaur's discard.

v1_map_disagreements.why: The six mana creatures form their own city (city-5), and all six are ramp:dork and threat:body bodies; only Atzocan Seer carries 'recursion'. The label is a uniqueness fallback, not a reading: Bodies and Ramp, the city's two top families, were already taken by the larger cities 0 and 1, so it got the next unclaimed name (deck_map unique_names). The cost reducers sit with other 'Dinosaur spells you cast' text in Ramp, and the land-search sorceries with tutors on 'search your library'. What they share, paying for Gishath, is not in any one card's text.

Only four of its fourteen cards are mana (Hunting Velociraptor, Knight of the Stampede, Otepec Huntmaster, Urza's Incubator). The rest are protection (Devil Dinosaur, Temple Altisaur, Kinjalli's Sunwing), win conditions (Carnage Tyrant, Ghalta, Overwhelming Stampede, Regal Imperiosaur), Blasphemous Act, Berserkers' Onslaught and Roaming Throne. The city reads as statics about Dinosaurs or costs, and its label follows the four.
The engine starts on a combat event, a hit, and the cards that make it count twice or bigger are an enchantment, a land and a copy creature. No text is shared, so the map cannot see the stage at all.

The declared kit is about haste for the 7/6, but Gishath already has haste. Four of its seven members grant haste to OTHER Dinosaurs or reduce costs, so the group scatters because it mixes three jobs (proposed_goldfish_edits[0]).
Removal on a Dinosaur body clusters as a body, which is the point: a reveal can deliver Bronzebeak, Itzquinth, Brontodon or Frillback for free, where Swords and Path cannot be revealed.

v1_map_disagreements.component: KEEPING THE BOARD THROUGH THE ANSWER
v1_map_disagreements.why: The five protection spells agree with Insurance. The three permanents doing the same job on a body (Devil Dinosaur's hexproof, Temple Altisaur's prevention, Kinjalli's Sunwing's tapped entries) are statics and land in Ramp.
Pumps, lords, haste-granters and fat tramplers share a job (a lethal swing) but no text; Rydia's Return lands in Tutors on its regrowth mode.
